question: What did Katie Hobbs do for the state of Arizona in the last 12 months?
subject: ballot-az-pima:governor|Katie Hobbs
visibleText:
Katie Hobbs · Governor

From the records we hold, Katie Hobbs — the sitting Governor of Arizona — signed six executive orders in the past 12 months: Protecting Arizonans' Healthcare Freedom (Sept. 11, 2025), Removing Barriers to Delivering Affordable Energy for Arizona (Sept. 15, 2025), Granting Authority to the Arizona Department of Homeland Security to Receive Criminal History Record Information (Nov. 5, 2025), Cutting Taxes for Hard-Working Arizonans (Nov. 25, 2025), Protecting Paychecks for Hard-Working Arizonans (May 20, 2026), and Protecting the Public Trust by Prohibiting State Government Workers from Using Nonpublic Information for Personal Profit (July 8, 2026). Her office's own site also references a 2026 State of the State address, erasing about $1 billion in medical debt, a memorandum of understanding with the Navajo Nation, and a statement on the Colorado River, though we hold no detail beyond those headlines. Two gaps on our side: we have not recorded bills she signed or vetoed, because the legislature's bill-status system can't be read automatically, and we read only 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, so there may be more actions past what we walked. She has also filed as a Democrat for Governor on the November 3, 2026 ballot.

These are executive orders only. We have not recorded bills signed or vetoed — the legislature's bill-status system does not permit automated reading, so that half of the record is not ours to show yet.

We read 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, and the index continues past what we walked.

Katie Hobbs · Governor

Katie Hobbs is Arizona's governor (Democratic) and has filed to run for Governor again in the November 3, 2026 general election. In the past 12 months, the actions we have on file are six executive orders: "Protecting Arizonans' Healthcare Freedom" (Sept 11, 2025), "Removing Barriers to Delivering Affordable Energy for Arizona" (Sept 15, 2025), one granting the Arizona Department of Homeland Security authority to receive criminal history record information (Nov 5, 2025), "Cutting Taxes for Hard-Working Arizonans" (Nov 25, 2025), "Protecting Paychecks for Hard-Working Arizonans" (May 20, 2026), and "Protecting the Public Trust by Prohibiting State Government Workers from Using Nonpublic Information for Personal Profit" (July 8, 2026). Her office's website also references items such as a memorandum of understanding with the Navajo Nation on economic matters, erasing about $1 billion in medical debt, a statement on the Colorado River, and a 2026 State of the State address, though we do not have dated records for those. Two gaps on our side: these are executive orders only — we have not recorded bills signed or vetoed, because the legislature's bill-status system can't be read automatically — and we read 12 of the 37 executive orders we indexed, so the list may be incomplete.

Andy Biggs · Governor

Our records show only one thing about Andy Biggs: he filed as a Republican candidate for Governor, according to the Arizona Secretary of State's candidate filing list. Governor is on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot, where voters choose one for a four-year term; the filing does not say whether he is the incumbent. The list we have covers everyone who filed for the July 21, 2026 primary — the Secretary of State has not yet published the general-election candidate list, which will narrow this to the nominees. We have not recorded any sourced statement of his positions.
